groups.defect: After taking the write lock in GetWebAssets, the code does not check the cache again, so concurrent first callers each rebuild it. The cache is also assigned when the load fails, so a nil or failed result can be stored and served.

answer.reasoning: Both suggestions point at the same write-lock section of GetWebAssets (lines 48 onward). Both report the same two defects: (1) the cache is not checked again after Lock(), and (2) the cache is assigned even when err != nil. Both propose the same fix: check the cache again after Lock() and assign it only when err == nil. So they are clearly duplicates of each other, and the grouping is settled. The judges disagreed only on needsUnifiedComment. Each member already covers both defects at the same place, so either one alone can replace the group without losing anything. A merged comment would not need to say more than any single member, which makes needsUnifiedComment false. The rule's wording about overlapping groups that report more than one defect could be read the other way, so this flag is a judgment call. That is why decisive is false.
